about: Idioms for characters to use, one a visit, glossed with the picture then the meaning (docs/mix.md → Idioms; Josh, 2026-11-13: "Idioms stick", "we might favor shotter and common", "start the list and I'll get youo edits later"). Chosen from idioms read out of Must-Know Italian Slang, Talk Like an Italian, 1001 Easy Italian Phrases, Les 800 expressions pour tout dire en italien, four modi di dire collections, Un tesoro di lingua and Los dichos de Jesús: common, 2 to 6 words, not already in syllabus.json, plus common biblical sayings. Only the idioms come from the books; pictures, meanings, situations and origins are our own words (origins are often folk etymology: stories, not facts). Not checked by a person yet: Josh's edits to come. common: very common | common; group: idiom | biblical.

idioms.meaning: to talk nonsense, to lose it; a machine acting up
idioms.fits: the ticket machine misbehaves; someone says something absurd

idioms.meaning: to go to ruin, fall apart
idioms.fits: a business, a plan, a relationship

idioms.meaning: to come to nothing (money, plans, work)
idioms.fits: a cancelled trip, a failed deal, a ruined harvest

idioms.picture: to have a tail of straw (it catches fire easily)

idioms.picture: to have a nail fixed in

idioms.meaning: to come at exactly the right moment

idioms.meaning: how boring, what a drag

idioms.picture: to cost an eye out of your head

idioms.picture: in a blink of the eye

idioms.picture: the habit doesn't make the monk

idioms.text: non avere né capo né coda

idioms.meaning: to come away with nothing

idioms.meaning: in episodes, bit by bit (a series, a story)

idioms.meaning: keep it quiet, mum's the word

idioms.meaning: happening all the time, routine

idioms.picture: in the light of the sun

idioms.meaning: to drink too much

idioms.meaning: to shout, speak angrily

idioms.meaning: go to ruin, be wasted or lost

idioms.meaning: sell out fast, be snapped up

idioms.meaning: to be proud, have nothing to be ashamed of
idioms.fits: encouraging a friend after a setback

idioms.text: andare all'aria / a monte (mandare all'aria, mandare a monte)

idioms.picture: to go in love and agreement

idioms.meaning: to be mad about
idioms.fits: football, gelato, a singer

idioms.meaning: wholeheartedly, totally

idioms.picture: to have your heart in your throat

idioms.meaning: have endless patience

idioms.text: avere la testa fra le nuvole

idioms.meaning: to be unable to act

idioms.meaning: to be completely wrong
idioms.fits: an argument about football or directions

idioms.picture: to have a devil for every hair

idioms.fits: after a traffic jam, a bad day

idioms.picture: to have a cat to skin

idioms.picture: to have it up above your hair
idioms.meaning: to be sick and tired of something

idioms.meaning: serves you right

idioms.picture: to throw money out of the window
idioms.meaning: to waste money

idioms.meaning: to be completely surprised by news everyone else already knew
idioms.fits: hearing a piece of local news for the first time

idioms.meaning: fit perfectly

idioms.meaning: get it instantly
idioms.fits: a barman grasping a quick order

idioms.picture: to look for a hair in the egg

idioms.meaning: persistence pays off
idioms.fits: encouraging someone who's struggling, a learner

idioms.meaning: be happy with what you have

idioms.meaning: to turn a blind eye, let it go

idioms.meaning: just what we needed (ironic, at one more problem). Don't mix up with *ci mancherebbe (altro)!*, "of course!"

idioms.text: cogliere (prendere) con le mani nel sacco
idioms.picture: to catch with your hands in the sack

idioms.picture: with the good sense of afterwards

idioms.fits: looking back on a decision

idioms.meaning: a chill caught from a draught
idioms.fits: a grandmother warning to close the window

idioms.meaning: love at first sight
idioms.fits: how a couple met; falling for a town

idioms.meaning: a sudden plot twist, surprising turn of events
idioms.fits: gossip at the market taking an unexpected turn

idioms.meaning: a quick phone call

idioms.meaning: a rash, impulsive decision

idioms.picture: with the tail of the eye
idioms.meaning: out of the corner of one's eye

idioms.meaning: routine, nothing special

idioms.meaning: to sleep on it

idioms.meaning: to be over the moon

idioms.meaning: to be capable, smart, on the ball; "in gamba!" also means take care, get well

idioms.text: essere in un mare di guai

idioms.picture: to bring the little water to your mouth

idioms.meaning: give goosebumps from fear, cold or emotion

idioms.text: chi è senza peccato scagli la prima pietra

idioms.text: vedere la pagliuzza nell'occhio altrui (e non la trave nel proprio)

idioms.text: il figliol prodigo (è tornato il figliol prodigo)

idioms.fits: the last to arrive gets served first

idioms.picture: nobody is a prophet in his own land

idioms.text: molti sono i chiamati, pochi gli eletti

idioms.text: chi ha orecchie per intendere, intenda

idioms.text: non sappia la tua sinistra ciò che fa la destra / la destra non sa cosa fa la sinistra

idioms.picture: for the centuries of the centuries

idioms.fits: a queue or a building project that never ends
idioms.origin: the closing formula of biblical praise (Galatians, Revelation) and of prayers

idioms.meaning: someone who has strayed from family or group

idioms.text: guadagnarsi il pane col sudore della fronte

idioms.meaning: to be cold, unmoved by others' pain

idioms.picture: turning into a pillar of salt
idioms.meaning: to be frozen with shock

idioms.meaning: a place of wild excess and vice
idioms.fits: a wild party, a rowdy nightlife street
idioms.origin: Genesis 19: two cities destroyed for their wickedness
